active.name: Meridian 2.4 m Optical Telescope
active.limitations: Cannot see through dense dust, so the Galactic Centre and distant compact objects are out of reach. Exoplanets can only be studied through their host stars at this stage.
active.description: A segmented-mirror optical telescope on a deployable boom, tuned for stellar photometry and imaging of nearby objects.

active.name: Halcyon 15 m Radio Dish
active.limitations: Poor angular resolution. Only nearby stars and bright radio sources are practical targets. Cannot reach very distant quasars.
active.description: A steerable dish with cryogenically cooled receivers. Radio waves pass through interstellar dust, which makes it the first instrument able to listen to the Galactic Centre.

planned.name: Infrared Telescope
planned.note: Will see through dust and observe cool objects.

planned.name: X-ray Observatory
planned.note: Will observe accretion disks and hot gas around compact objects.

planned.name: Gamma-ray Detector
planned.note: Will monitor bursts and extreme events.

planned.name: Neutrino Detector
planned.note: Will observe supernova neutrinos and the solar interior.

planned.name: Gravitational-wave Observatory
planned.note: Will detect mergers of compact objects.

planned.name: Spectrometer Suite
planned.note: Will measure composition and exoplanet atmospheres.

planned.name: Deep-space Sensor Array
planned.note: Will combine instruments for long-baseline observations.
